species: Human ovarian cancer cell lines, including ES-2 (ATCC, Manassas, VA, USA), SKOV3 (ATCC, Manassas, VA, USA), and OVTW59 (a kind gift from Dr. P. L. Tong, Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology, National Taiwan University), were maintained in Dulbecco’s modified Eagle’s medium (DMEM) (Invitrogen, Grand Island, NY, USA) supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum (Gibco, Gaithersburg, MD, USA).
tissue: TMTC1 was overexpressed in ovarian cancer tissues compared with adjacent normal ovarian tissues, and high TMTC1 expression was associated with poor prognosis in patients with ovarian cancer.
cell_type: TMTC1 promotes invasiveness of ovarian cancer cells through integrins β1 and β4
disease_state: Ovarian cancer is the most lethal gynecological malignancy and is characterized by peritoneal disseminated metastasis.
sample_source: In addition, we examined TMTC1 levels in a tissue microarray (Biomax BC11115c) using immunohistochemical staining.
age: Female BALB/cAnN.Cg-Foxnlnu/CrlNarl nude mice aged between 5 and 7 weeks were procured from the National Laboratory Animal Center, Taiwan.
anatomic_site_tumor: The results showed that TMTC1 overexpression increased tumor weights and the number of tumor nodules in the peritoneal cavity (Fig. 6B, C).
cell_line: SKOV3 cells had the highest TMTC1 level followed by OVTW59 cells, whereas ES-2 cells had the lowest TMTC1 level (Supplementary Fig. S2).
sex: Female BALB/cAnN.Cg-Foxnlnu/CrlNarl nude mice aged between 5 and 7 weeks were procured from the National Laboratory Animal Center, Taiwan.
